questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis in a Two-Dimensional Vector Space
questions.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,$ $T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 5 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & -7 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -18 & -46 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-18 & -46 \\ 7 & 18\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Images of the Basis Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
Since we have $\,T({b}_{1})=3{b}_{2}-4{b}_{1}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=3{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}\,$, we have

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis in a Three-Dimensional Vector Space
questions.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 5 \\ -3 & b & -5 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+y+z \\ x-y \\ x-z\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -3 & -1 & -10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 5 \\ -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=3,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=3+(-2)+(-2)=-1.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis in a Three-Dimensional Vector Space
questions.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ a & b & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x-z \\ x+y \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 8 & -2 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 8 & -2 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & 2 & -2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=\frac{1}{4},$ $b=-\frac{1}{4},$ $c=1$ and 

$$
a+b+c=\frac{1}{4}+(-\frac{1}{4})+1=1.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis in a Two-Dimensional Vector Space
questions.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 26\end{aligned}],\,$ $T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -13\end{aligned}],\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 11 & -4 \\ 2 & 5 & 26 & -13\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 11 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 4 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$
